_what: Questions 1, 2 and 4 of `docs/pine/r11-time-and-valuewhen.md` — what `time(<timeframe>)` returns — read off a live TradingView chart on 1D.
_ruling: ⭐⭐ `time("W")` IS NEVER `na`, AND IT RETURNS THE FORMING WEEK'S OPEN — the third of the three candidates the doc listed, not the two anybody was choosing between. `time(timeframe.period)` is exactly `time`. And `time("D") != time("D")[1]` is true on every bar of a 1D chart, so the classic new-period idiom works.

Q1_higher_timeframe_with_no_bar.question: On a bar where the higher timeframe has no bar (a 1D chart asking time("W") mid-week), does it return na, the open time of the FORMING higher-timeframe bar, or the LAST COMPLETED one?
Q1_higher_timeframe_with_no_bar.ruling: The FORMING bar's open. Never na.
Q1_higher_timeframe_with_no_bar._how_to_read_it: ⭐ THE OFFSET SET IS THE PROOF, and it is why the probe plots a delta in days rather than a flag. `time("W")` sits 0 to 4 days BEFORE the bar reading it — exactly the distance from a weekday back to that same week's Monday open. If it were the LAST COMPLETED week the offsets would be 5 to 9 days; if it were na there would be na bars. Neither appears.

Q2_chart_own_timeframe.question: Is time(timeframe.period) exactly `time`, or can it differ at a session edge?
Q2_chart_own_timeframe._how_to_read_it: The na-flag is reported beside the delta on purpose: 'equal' and 'both missing' are the same zero otherwise, and a session edge is exactly where a difference would hide.

Q4_new_period_idiom.question: Does `time("D") != time("D")[1]` — the classic new-day test — work?
Q4_new_period_idiom.ruling: True on every bar of a 1D chart, with no na anywhere.
Q4_new_period_idiom._and_the_precondition_HOLDS: ⭐ The doc made this conditional: the idiom 'would be a cheap win — but only if (1) is na-free'. Q1 says it is. So the condition is satisfied and the idiom is available.
